explanation: A triumph is a great success or win; victory.
distractor_rationales: wisdom — good judgment gained from experience; a triumph is a win, not a quality of mind
trickery — dishonest scheming; a triumph need involve no deception
theft — the act of stealing; unrelated to winning

explanation: To soar is to fly or climb high; rise.
distractor_rationales: steal — to take what is not yours; nothing to do with climbing upward
tease — to make fun of someone; a social act, not upward motion
shout — to call out loudly; a sound, not a movement upward

explanation: Merit is the quality of deserving praise; worth.
distractor_rationales: tribute — an act or gift showing respect; it is given to merit, it is not merit itself
shyness — a lack of confidence; not a quality of deserving
outrage — strong anger at an injustice; unrelated to deserving praise

explanation: To observe is to see and pay attention to; notice.
distractor_rationales: seize — to take hold of by force; observing involves no taking
request — to ask for something; observing asks for nothing
roam — to wander without a fixed path; a kind of travel, not attention

explanation: The zenith is the highest point of something; peak.
distractor_rationales: trace — a small remaining sign of something; a remnant, not a high point
start — the beginning of something; a zenith is a high point, not a beginning
mistake — an error; unrelated to a highest point

explanation: To oust is to force out of a position; remove.
distractor_rationales: nurture — to care for and help grow; the opposite of pushing someone out
tempt — to attract someone toward something; drawing in, not pushing out
resist — to hold out against force; ousting is applying force, not holding out

explanation: A malady is a disease or ailment; sickness.
distractor_rationales: talent — a natural ability; not an ailment
uproar — loud confusion and disorder; a disturbance, not an illness
wrath — intense anger; a feeling, not a disease

explanation: To mar is to damage or impair the look or quality of something; spoil.
distractor_rationales: nag — to pester repeatedly; annoying a person, not damaging a thing
yearn — to long for something; a desire, not damage
rejoice — to feel or show great joy; unrelated to damaging

explanation: Remorse is deep sorrow for a wrong one has done; regret.
distractor_rationales: surprise — the feeling at something unexpected; not sorrow for a wrong
nonsense — foolish talk; not a feeling at all
promise — a pledge to do something; not a feeling of sorrow

explanation: To satiate is to fill an appetite or desire completely; satisfy.
distractor_rationales: worship — to honor deeply; has nothing to do with filling a need
trouble — to disturb or upset; does not fill a desire
punish — to make someone suffer for wrongdoing; unrelated to appetite

explanation: A malevolent person wishes harm to others; wicked.
distractor_rationales: rowdy — noisy and rough; loud behavior, not ill will
nosy — too interested in others' affairs; prying, not wishing harm
rash — acting without thought; haste, not ill will

explanation: Something poignant stirs sad or tender feelings; touching.
distractor_rationales: massive — extremely large; size, not emotional effect
moral — right and good in conduct; a judgment of conduct, not feeling
mighty — very strong or powerful; force, not emotional effect

explanation: A vocation is the work a person does for a living; occupation.
distractor_rationales: nobility — the high-ranking class of a society; a social rank, not one's work
reputation — what people generally think of someone; not one's work
tradition — a long-established practice; a habit of a group, not a job

explanation: A sagacious person shows sound judgment; wise.
distractor_rationales: shy — lacking confidence among others; a temperament, not good judgment
tame — easily controlled or gentle; obedience, not wisdom
picky — very hard to please; fussiness, not wisdom

explanation: A proclivity is a natural inclination to behave a certain way; tendency.
distractor_rationales: variety — a range of different things; not an inclination
monotony — dull sameness; boredom, not an inclination
vigor — physical or mental energy; strength, not inclination

explanation: Something tortuous is full of twists and turns; winding.
distractor_rationales: spotless — perfectly clean; cleanliness, not shape
rotten — decayed and foul-smelling; condition, not shape
shiny — giving off a soft gleam; appearance of light, not shape

explanation: A profligate person spends recklessly; wasteful.
distractor_rationales: shameful — bringing disgrace; dishonor, not spending
mindful — careful and aware; if anything the opposite of reckless spending
playful — full of fun; high spirits, not spending
